artworks.title: Erysichthon Sells His Daughter Mestra
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum oil: Steen stages Ovid's cruel sequel — Erysichthon, wasting under Demeter's hunger-curse, sells shape-shifting Mestra for food. Sacrilege rewritten as market-day desperation.

artworks.title: Ceres' Nymph Telling Famine to Strike Erysichthon
artworks.description: Tempesta Metamorphoses plate (MET): Ceres' nymph carries the order that Famine enter Erysichthon's vitals — the divine machinery that turns the felled oak into endless appetite.

artworks.title: Erysichthon Selling His Daughter
artworks.description: Plate 81 of the same cycle: Mestra sold again and again in shifting guise while her father eats through every ransom — appetite that consumes the household.

artworks.title: Erysichthon and Mestra
artworks.description: Baur's Metamorphoses etching: Erysichthon bargains over Mestra while Ceres' hunger still claws at him — seventeenth-century print culture's stock image of the Thessalian curse.
